meta.comment: engine.traffic (planned MOD) inc0 table: safe-road score and integration score inputs and weights, feeding wellbeing/tourism/attract per inc9's stated scope. This file defines the SCORING INPUTS and WEIGHTS only -- wiring the score into wellbeing/tourism is inc9's engine work, out of inc0's data-only scope (GR#25: no speculative cross-module edge is proposed here, only a data table a future registered interface may consume).

safeRoadScore.$comment: Per-segment safety score in [0,1], 1 = safest. Weighted combination of road class, junction type, design speed, and current v/c (a high-v/c congested segment is both slower AND has a different, generally lower per-vehicle-km casualty rate than free-flow high-speed roads -- real-world road-safety literature shows speed is the dominant severity driver, congestion the dominant frequency driver, so both terms are carried, not conflated).

components.note: Per-class base safety index, informed by UK STATS19 casualty-rate-by-road-type order-of-magnitude (motorways lowest casualty rate per vehicle-km despite highest speed, due to grade separation; unclassified/local roads and junctions show the highest casualty rate per vehicle-km).
components.source: derived approximation, order-of-magnitude informed by UK DfT STATS19 reported-casualty-rate-by-road-type statistics

components.note: Grade-separated/roundabout junctions materially outperform simple priority/signal junctions in casualty rate (UK STATS19 junction-type breakdown, order-of-magnitude).
components.source: derived approximation, UK DfT STATS19 order-of-magnitude

components.note: Higher design/actual speed raises casualty SEVERITY even where frequency is lower (UK DfT: casualty severity rises sharply above ~30-40km/h in mixed-traffic environments, the core justification for 20mph/30km/h urban zones). Penalty = max(0, (speedKmh-30)/100), clamped to [0,1].
components.source: UK DfT 20mph/30km/h zone casualty-severity evaluation literature, order-of-magnitude

components.note: Sustained high v/c (>0.9) is associated with higher LOW-speed shunt-type incident frequency even as severity falls; small negative safety contribution at extreme congestion, distinct from the emergency-response speed-degradation curve in emergency_response.json (that curve is about ACCESS time, this is about incident RATE).

integratedTransportScore.$comment: Per-tile or per-district integration score in [0,1] rewarding interchange adjacency and mode-share balance, per Aaron's brief ('reward integrated transport') and inc9's stated design intent (interchange adjacency + mode-share balance).

components.note: Fraction of the population within a walkable radius (placeholder 400m, ~5min walk at modes.json walk speed 5km/h, referenced not restated) of a stop/station offering 2+ distinct modes (e.g. bus+metro, or metro+heavy_rail).

walkAccessRadiusM.source: UK/international standard walk-catchment radius for a 5-minute walk at typical pedestrian speed (widely used transit-planning convention, e.g. TfL's own PTAL methodology catchment radii)

components.note: Shannon-entropy-style evenness measure over the realised mode-share vector (scale_ladder.json modeShare for the relevant density band): balance = -sum(share_i * ln(share_i)) / ln(11), normalised to [0,1] where 1 = perfectly even split across all 11 modes and 0 = single-mode monoculture. Rewards a city that has GENUINE modal choice, not merely 'high transit share' (a city 100% dependent on one metro line scores lower than one with a healthy walk/cycle/bus/metro mix even at similar aggregate transit share).
components.source: Shannon entropy, standard information-theoretic evenness measure (literature: Shannon, C.E. (1948), A Mathematical Theory of Communication) applied here as this schema's own mode-balance metric, not a transcribed transport-planning citation
components.confidenceNote: the entropy FORMULA is a standard literature citation; its application as a transport 'integration score' is this schema's own design choice

provenance.source: UK DfT STATS19 casualty-rate order-of-magnitude, UK 20mph zone evaluation literature, Shannon (1948) entropy formula (literature), TfL PTAL-style walk-catchment convention
provenance.note: Weights (0.35/0.25/0.20/0.20 and 0.5/0.5) are this schema's own directional allocation, not fitted to any dataset -- pending Aaron's balance pass. No engine wiring is proposed by this file (GR#25); it is a data proposal for inc9.
